children: Samoa's economic growth is expected to slow sharply in the fiscal year ending June 2026, as weaker domestic demand, subdued agriculture and commerce, and higher fuel and shipping costs weigh on the Pacific island nation, the International Monetary Fund said on Thursday.
The IMF projected real gross domestic product growth of 0.4% in 2025/26, from 4.2% in the previous fiscal year, following a strong post-pandemic recovery.
Growth is forecast to recover to 2.0% in 2026/27 and settle at about 2.5% over the medium term.
The Fund said Samoa's low public debt, strong foreign-exchange reserves and prudent policymaking had helped it absorb external shocks.
Tourism and remittances continued to support the external position, it said.
Inflation is expected to accelerate to an average 4.5% in 2026/27 from 1.4% estimated in 2025/26, as higher fuel and food prices filter through the economy.
IMF directors said Samoa should use available fiscal space to cushion vulnerable households from the energy shock, but ensure assistance is temporary, transparent and targeted.
They also urged stronger public-investment management, a sufficiently tight monetary stance and reforms to address labour shortages, infrastructure gaps and the narrow production base.
